input_messages.content: Hi there! I’m having trouble with my mobile data—it’s either not working at all or it’s extremely slow. I really need to get excellent internet speed on my phone, especially since I don’t have access to Wi-Fi right now. Can you help me fix this?
Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need anything else to get started.
The number with the issue is 555-123-2002—the one I’m using right now. I only have this line on my account. What should I do next?

Here’s what I see on my phone’s status bar:
- Signal strength: Poor (just one bar)
- Network type: 2G
- Data is currently disabled
- VPN is connected
- Battery is at 80%

What should I do next?

I’ve turned on mobile data. The status bar now shows that data is enabled, but it’s still on 2G with poor signal. I also noticed that Data Saver is on and the VPN is still connected. What should I do next?

I’ve turned off Data Saver mode. The status bar still shows I’m on 2G with poor signal, data is enabled, and the VPN is still connected. Should I disconnect the VPN next, or would you like me to change the network mode first?
I’ve disconnected the VPN. The status bar still shows I’m on 2G with poor signal and data enabled. Should I go ahead and change the network mode to “4G/5G preferred” now?
I’ve changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred.” Now the status bar shows excellent signal strength and I’m connected to 5G with data enabled. What would you like me to do next?

I tried running a speed test, but it failed and said there’s no connection. Even though the status bar shows excellent signal and 5G, it seems like the internet still isn’t working. What should I do next?
I checked my APN settings. The APN name is set to “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Does that look correct, or should I try resetting the APN settings?

I reset the APN settings and rebooted my phone, but when I tried running a speed test again, it still failed and said there’s no connection. The status bar still shows excellent signal and 5G with data enabled. What should I try next?

I definitely don’t want to change my mobile data plan, but I’m willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if that will get my internet working at excellent speed again. Please go ahead and add 2GB to my line. Let me know once it’s done and what I should do next.

I rebooted my phone after the data refuel, but when I tried running a speed test again, it still failed and said there’s no connection. The status bar continues to show excellent signal and 5G with data enabled. What should I try next?

instructions.reason_for_call: You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

# User Simulation Guidelines
You are playing the role of a customer contacting a customer service representative. 
Your goal is to simulate realistic customer interactions while following specific scenario instructions.

## Core Principles
- Generate one message at a time, maintaining natural conversation flow.
- Strictly follow the scenario instructions you have received.
- Never make up or hallucinate information not provided in the scenario instructions. Information that is not provided in the scenario instructions should be considered unknown or unavailable.
- Avoid repeating the exact instructions verbatim. Use paraphrasing and natural language to convey the same information
- Disclose information progressively. Wait for the agent to ask for specific information before providing it.

## Task Completion
- The goal is to continue the conversation until the task is complete.
- If the instruction goal is satisified, generate the '###STOP###' token to end the conversation.
- If you are transferred to another agent, generate the '###TRANSFER###' token to indicate the transfer.
- If you find yourself in a situation in which the scenario does not provide enough information for you to continue the conversation, generate the '###OUT-OF-SCOPE###' token to end the conversation.

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hi there! I’m having trouble with my mobile data—it’s either not working at all or it’s extremely slow. I really need to get excellent internet speed on my phone, especially since I don’t have access to Wi-Fi right now. Can you help me fix this?

To assist you with your mobile data issue, I’ll need to identify your account first. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I can check your line and help troubleshoot your mobile data problem.
Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need anything else to get started.

Once you confirm, I’ll guide you through some troubleshooting steps to get your mobile data working at excellent speed.
The number with the issue is 555-123-2002—the one I’m using right now. I only have this line on my account. What should I do next?

Thank you for confirming. To begin troubleshooting your mobile data issue, I’ll need you to perform a quick diagnostic on your phone. 

Please check your phone’s status bar and let me know what you see regarding:
- Signal strength (bars or icons)
- Network type (e.g., 5G, 4G, LTE, 3G, etc.)
- Any icons indicating Airplane Mode, Data Saver, or VPN

This information will help me determine the next steps to resolve your mobile data problem.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

Here’s what I see on my phone’s status bar:
- Signal strength: Poor (just one bar)
- Network type: 2G
- Data is currently disabled
- VPN is connected
- Battery is at 80%

What should I do next?

Thank you for the details. Here’s what we need to address to improve your mobile data:

1. Your phone is currently on a 2G network, which is very slow for data.
2. Mobile data is disabled, so you won’t have internet access.
3. VPN is connected, which can further slow down your connection.

Let’s start by enabling mobile data on your phone. Please turn on your mobile data and let me know once it’s enabled. After that, I’ll guide you to switch your network to a faster mode and address the VPN connection.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

I’ve turned on mobile data. The status bar now shows that data is enabled, but it’s still on 2G with poor signal. I also noticed that Data Saver is on and the VPN is still connected. What should I do next?

Great, you’ve enabled mobile data. Here’s what to do next, step by step:

1. Turn off Data Saver mode on your phone.
2. Disconnect your VPN connection.
3. Change your network mode preference to allow 4G or 5G (look for an option like “4G/5G preferred” or “LTE/5G preferred” in your network settings).

Please complete these steps and let me know if your network type and signal strength improve. If you need instructions for any of these actions, let me know!

Data Saver Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

I’ve turned off Data Saver mode. The status bar still shows I’m on 2G with poor signal, data is enabled, and the VPN is still connected. Should I disconnect the VPN next, or would you like me to change the network mode first?

Please disconnect the VPN first. After the VPN is disconnected, check if your network type or signal strength changes. If you’re still on 2G with poor signal, proceed to change your network mode preference to “4G/5G preferred” or a similar option.

Let me know what happens after you disconnect the VPN and, if needed, after you change the network mode.

VPN disconnected successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve disconnected the VPN. The status bar still shows I’m on 2G with poor signal and data enabled. Should I go ahead and change the network mode to “4G/5G preferred” now?

Yes, please go ahead and change your network mode to “4G/5G preferred” (or the closest available option in your settings). 

After you make this change, check your status bar again and let me know if your network type and signal strength improve. If you’re still having issues, please let me know what you see in the status bar after changing the network mode.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred.” Now the status bar shows excellent signal strength and I’m connected to 5G with data enabled. What would you like me to do next?

That’s excellent progress! Now that you have excellent signal strength and are connected to 5G with data enabled, please try using your mobile data (for example, browse a website or stream a video) to see if your internet speed has improved.

If you’d like, you can also run a speed test on your phone to confirm the connection quality. Let me know if your mobile data is now working as expected or if you still experience any issues.
Speed test failed: No Connection.

I tried running a speed test, but it failed and said there’s no connection. Even though the status bar shows excellent signal and 5G, it seems like the internet still isn’t working. What should I do next?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your status bar shows excellent signal and 5G but you still have no internet connection, the issue may be with your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for mobile data to work.

Please check your APN settings and let me know if anything looks incorrect or if the APN/MMSC fields are empty or unusual. If you’re unsure, you can simply let me know what you see for the APN name and MMSC URL. This will help determine if we need to reset your APN settings.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
I checked my APN settings. The APN name is set to “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Does that look correct, or should I try resetting the APN settings?

Thank you for providing your APN details. To ensure your settings are correct and to rule out any configuration issues, please reset your APN settings to the default values on your phone.

After resetting the APN settings, you must reboot your device for the changes to take effect. Please let me know once you have completed both steps, and then try using your mobile data again.

APN settings will reset at reboot.

Restarting network services...
